Just because you can update something because you personally think it’s better doesn’t mean the player base or community feels the same way. The redesign does nothing for the social tabs other than complicate the way things look, feel, and function. For a game named after talking and finding friends on a VR platform, the decision to add features that shouldn’t—and are not—the main focus of the gameplay leaves a bad aftertaste and an even worse outlook on the direction the developers are actively taking the game.

details:
The new profile themes allow users to choose arbitrary colors for text, buttons, icons, and backgrounds. Some combinations can make functional UI difficult or impossible to read, for example, white text on a bright yellow button.

This is primarily a readability and visual-comfort issue. Poor contrast can affect users with low vision, color-vision deficiencies, migraines, light sensitivity, or other visual-processing difficulties. It can also be especially uncomfortable in VR headsets.

Please add an accessibility option that lets viewers override custom profile themes with VRChat's default colors. Ideally, this would include a global toggle to show/hide custom profile themes, automatic use of default colors when a high-contrast accessibility mode is enabled, or contrast validation in the theme editor to prevent unreadable combinations.

Profile customization is a nice form of self-expression, but the viewer's accessibility and readability preferences should take priority over another user's theme.
title: [1878] Let users override or disable custom profile themes for accessibility
